newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares driven higher by Salus rebound.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares driven higher by Salus rebound.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose in meagre volume on Thursday, boosted by a rebound in drug wholesaler Salus and a technical correction, traders said.

"Prices, also in Salus were already very low, so today's rise was an expected correction to previous levels and probably nothing more, but there could be some turnaround after the May holidays" said Andrej Kavcic, a trader of brokerage Ilirika.
The SBI index firmed 0.28 percent or 3.65 points to 1,309.47, ending a four-day losing streak.
Turnover slumped to 29.3 million tolars from 46.6 million tolars. Overall eight shares rose, seven fell and two were flat, while 10 were untraded.
Drug producer Lek's A issue had the highest turnover, firming 0.45 percent to 24,710 tolars on volume of 249 shares for total turnover of 6.1 million tolars.
Salus was the top gainer, jumping 6.33 percent to 13,110 tolars on volume of 100 shares for total turnover of 1.3 million tolars.
Bank Probanka led the day's decliners, falling 2.96 percent to 19,310 tolars on volume of 54 shares.
